messages:
Maya (CSM): Heads-up — Kestrel (renewal in 3 weeks) flagged a sustained latency regression last week, asking about credits and whether onboarding work covered it. Can we triage?
Diego (Support): Seeing increased p50/p95 for their dedicated pool from 120ms -> 420ms between Tue-Thu. No full outages, but spikes during peak traffic. Digging into model routing.
Priya (Onboarding): Thanks. Did their rollout pin to the older quantized variant? We suggested the newer q4 profile during onboarding but left it optional.
Diego (Support): They were on model:v2-q8 by commit id. I can confirm requests were routed to fallback instances during node drains — warmup not fully primed.
Maya (CSM): Customer expects clarity on uptime vs latency SLOs and whether they qualify for a credit under their contract. We should prepare an evidence bundle + timeline and a mitigation plan.
Jonah (Solutions): I can scope a remediation doc: quick wins are (1) bump q-profile to v3-q4 where latency stable, (2) pre-warm KV cache and set min-instances=2 for peak hours, (3) enable prefix caching for repeated prompts.
Priya (Onboarding): I'll own the pre-warm/playbook doc and run a 30-min enablement with their infra team this week.
Diego (Support): Attaching snippet of the rolling window that shows the latency delta (copied from monitoring):
```
2026-03-10T10:00Z p95=420ms pool=kestrel-dedicated-01
2026-03-11T14:00Z p95=390ms pool=kestrel-dedicated-01
2026-03-12T02:00Z p95=130ms pool=kestrel-dedicated-01
```
Maya (CSM): For the customer-facing note, we need: incident summary (what, when, impact), root cause hypothesis, mitigation applied, timeline of actions, and whether credit applies per SLA clause 3.2. Also include instructions they can follow to avoid recurrence.
Diego (Support): Root cause: warmup + rolling drains triggered fallbacks to smaller instances causing higher tail latency. We reverted the node draining policy for that pool and rebalanced traffic — seeing p95 back at ~140ms now.
OpsBot: alert: Kestrel-dedicated-01 rolling-drain detected (auto-posted by infra-monitor).
Jonah (Solutions): Draft of customer message (short): "We observed increased request latency due to rolling drains on your dedicated pool, causing fallback to capacity with higher tail latency. We rebalanced traffic and adjusted drain policy; latency is back to baseline. We'll partner to pre-warm & set min-instances for your peak.":+1:
Maya (CSM): Please assemble the evidence bundle: monitoring graphs, the raw p95 times, list of affected windows, and the config changes we applied. Diego, can you drop the Prometheus query/links?
Diego (Support): Prom query: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool))` with pool="kestrel-dedicated-01" and time range 2026-03-09..2026-03-13. I'll export graphs and attach to the ticket.
Priya (Onboarding): I'll schedule the 30-min enablement on Wed 11am PT and include a short playbook PDF.
Maya (CSM): Owner/next steps: Diego = evidence export + credit calc; Priya = enablement + playbook; Jonah = customer note + config diff; Maya = coordinate renewal comms and finalize whether to offer credit.
Jonah (Solutions): Quick credit guideline: if SLO breach >0.5% of requests in billing window -> standard credit per SLA. Diego, can you quantify affected percent?
Diego (Support): Running estimate now — initial looks like ~1.6% of requests fell into the higher-latency windows across the billing period. I'll confirm in the ticket by EOD.
Maya (CSM): Great. I'll draft the renewal memo showing remediation and the enablement offer. Aim to have customer note + evidence bundle ready before Fri EOD.
Priya (Onboarding): I'll also add a section to the playbook on how to validate KV cache priming after deploys.
Maya (CSM): Thanks team — keeping this tight since renewal hangs on perceived reliability. Ping me if any blockers. :pray:
